name: Two-bowl pho
summary: Pleiku serves one portion as two bowls: thin rice noodles with toppings, and a clear broth you sip or pour. Go Vietnam calls the black fermented-soybean sauce the dry bowl. Printed portions run about 35,000–60,000 VND.
origin: Go Vietnam, 13 August 2026, places the dry bowl in Pleiku and traces the broth-apart style to the Teochew community that settled there around the 1950s and 1960s. VnExpress International records a 2012 Asian Records Organization listing, one of 10 Vietnamese dishes cited for Asian culinary value.
taste: Go Vietnam describes savory-sweet meat, crisp shallots and cracklings, and black sauce in the chewy noodles, against a clear, gently sweet broth.
Vietnam Tourism’s culinary journey calls the broth light and subtly sweet, with little seasoning, and the noodles ivory-white and chewy rather than translucent.
howToEat: Toss the dry bowl with the black sauce, herbs, lime, and chili, and sip the broth between bites. Go Vietnam also describes pouring some broth into the noodles.

Go Vietnam’s dry-bowl toppings are minced beef or shredded chicken, fried shallots, pork cracklings, and bean sprouts, finished with spring onion and cilantro. Lettuce, basil, lime, and chili come alongside.

VnExpress International prints fried pork fat, fried shallots, scallions, minced pork, beef or chicken, bean sprouts, basil, lettuce, coriander, and Gia Lai black sauce from fermented soybean. The broth is pork and beef bones, or chicken bones.
Go Vietnam’s broth is beef or chicken bones with charred ginger and charred onion, salt, and fish sauce, holding rare beef, beef balls, or chicken.
Vietnam.vn describes the noodles at one Nguyễn Văn Trỗi bowl as round, thin, and chewy.
where: Nguyễn Văn Trỗi in Pleiku is the street Go Vietnam names. Shops there run from early morning through midday, and some stay open all day. A single door’s clock is Check on arrival.
Vietnam.vn, 22 April 2026, puts the same bowl on Điện Hồng food street at night, on Nguyễn Thiện Thuật and Trần Phú in Điện Hồng ward. Stall hours are Check on arrival.
priceBand: Go Vietnam, 13 August 2026, prints a common 2025 range of 35,000–60,000 VND a portion, with Nguyễn Văn Trỗi examples around 35,000, 45,000–60,000, and about 60,000 VND. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism pho article prints about 35,000 VND a portion. Vietnam.vn prints 50,000 VND for one regular bowl on Nguyễn Văn Trỗi.
seoTitle: Two-bowl pho in Pleiku — dry noodles and a broth bowl
seoDescription: Pleiku’s phở hai tô is dry noodles and a separate broth, with black fermented-soybean sauce. Nguyễn Văn Trỗi by day. Prices in print run about 35,000–60,000 VND.
